module.clean.label: Clean
clean.title: Clean
clean.description: Fix what is wrong in the data, step by step. Each fix says why; the original is never changed: you save a cleaned version beside it.
clean.working.hint: Clean works on the dataset you have open. Pick another version in the top bar to clean that one instead.
clean.pins.title: Advanced · Pinned rows
clean.pins.hint: Turn the labels of pinned rows into a column
clean.pins.add: Add the labels as a column
clean.pins.added: The step is in the draft ({to}): save a version to get the column.
clean.pins.none: Pin rows first: on the Data page, in Unusual rows, or here by number.
clean.banner.label: Draft
clean.banner.noSteps: No step yet: tick a suggestion or add a step.
clean.layer.advancedHint: Clusters of spellings, values that depend on another column, units, near-duplicate rows.
clean.layer.expertHint: Slower, less common checks, run one by one: unusual rows, suspicious labels, empty cells filled for analysis, cell errors learnt from a few marks.
clean.layer.empty: Nothing to fix here: no rule found a problem.
clean.layer.advancedOpen: Computed when you open it: a few seconds.
clean.expert.intro: Methods that learn from the data. Nothing runs until you click Run, and a run can be stopped. What they find is only suggested: read why, then tick it yourself.
clean.expert.unusual_rows.title: Unusual rows
clean.expert.unusual_rows.hint: Rows unlike the others across their columns (Isolation Forest, as in Unusual rows). Mark them in a column, or remove them.
clean.expert.unusual_rows.cost: A few seconds, 200,000 rows at most.
clean.expert.suspicious_labels.title: Suspicious labels
clean.expert.suspicious_labels.hint: Rows whose label the other columns contradict with confidence (probabilities out of sample over 5 folds, confident learning). Relabel them or remove them.
clean.expert.suspicious_labels.cost: Up to half a minute, 50,000 rows at most.
clean.expert.fill_empty.title: Fill empty cells
clean.expert.fill_empty.hint: Empty numbers filled from the most similar rows, each value with its band. For the analysis only: for machine learning, let the ML preparation fill them inside each fold.
clean.expert.fill_empty.cost: A few seconds per column, 5,000 empty cells at most.
clean.expert.cell_errors.title: Cell errors from your marks
clean.expert.cell_errors.hint: Mark about twenty cells of a column Error or OK; the cells like your errors are found, each with a correction.
clean.expert.clearHint: Removes these results; the steps you ticked stay in the draft.
clean.expert.marks.title: Mark these cells
clean.expert.marks.hint: One cell for each group of similar cells. Mark at least one Error and one OK, then learn.
clean.expert.marks.label: Mark of row {row}
clean.flow.label: How to clean
clean.flow.reviewBody: {count} fixes found, grouped by what they change in the data.
clean.flow.reviewNone: Nothing to fix found by the rules.
clean.flow.saveHint: A new dataset beside this one, which stays as it is.
clean.group.format.hint: How values are written, never what they mean: spaces, invisible characters, encoding, HTML codes, a trailing '.0'.
clean.group.values.hint: Some values are replaced: spellings merged, words for 'missing' emptied, lost zeros restored.
clean.group.types.hint: A column is read as numbers, dates, true/false or text: its sums, charts and tests change.
clean.group.rows.hint: Rows are removed or merged: the row count changes.
clean.group.columns.hint: Columns are removed, split or renamed.
clean.group.decision.hint: Information could be lost, or it is a judgement call. Not ticked: read why, then tick what you agree with.
clean.groupBy.label: Group the fixes
clean.quality.title: Column quality
clean.quality.hint: {count} columns · {flagged} with cells to fix, empty or unreadable
clean.quality.partHint.valid: Read by the column's type, with no fix waiting
clean.quality.partHint.toFix: Changed by a fix you have not ticked yet
clean.quality.partHint.missing: No value, or a word read as empty (N/A, -)
clean.quality.partHint.unreadable: A value the column's type cannot read
clean.quality.fixed: {count} cells changed by the fixes ticked
clean.quality.uncounted: Unreadable values not counted: the column has too many distinct values.
clean.quality.once: A cell counts once: empty first, then unreadable, then to fix.
clean.quality.measured: Measured on the data as imported. Ticking a fix moves its cells out of "To fix"; nothing changes until you save a version.
clean.quality.caption: Quality of each column: cells and share of the rows
clean.quality.values: Values not read as {reading}, most rows first:
clean.quality.noFix: No fix waits for this column.
clean.facet.title: Facets
clean.facet.hint: A column's values and their rows; turn a selection into a step
clean.facet.onDraft: Read on the draft: every step applied. Nothing changes until you add a step.
clean.facet.sort.name: By name
clean.facet.listed: {shown} of {count} values: search to find the others
clean.facet.rangeHint: Click a bar to pick its range, Shift+click to extend it, or type the bounds.
clean.facet.none: Pick values, the blank or unreadable cells, or a range: the rows they pick are shown here.
clean.facet.picked: {rows} of {total} rows of the draft picked
clean.facet.actions: Turn the selection into a step
clean.facet.reason.merge: Merge {count} values into "{target}" in {column}: {rows} rows change.
clean.facet.reason.missing: Read {count} values as missing in {column}: {rows} cells become empty.
clean.facet.reason.missingOne: Read "{value}" as missing in {column}: {rows} cells become empty.
clean.facet.reason.remove: Remove the {rows} rows picked, of {total} in the draft.
clean.facet.reason.keep: Keep only the {rows} rows picked: {gone} rows are removed.
clean.facet.reason.outside: Empty the values of {column} outside {low} to {high}: {cells} cells become empty.
clean.facet.added: Step {id} added to the draft. Nothing changes in the data until you save a version.
clean.steps.label: Steps of the draft
clean.steps.empty: No step yet. Tick a suggestion, or add your own step.
clean.steps.pick: Pick a step to see its settings and what it changes.
clean.steps.off: This step is off: it is kept in the draft but does not run.
clean.catalog.title: Add a step
clean.op.keep_rows: Keep or remove the first or last rows
clean.op.promote_header: Use the first row as headers
clean.opHint.drop_columns: Leave columns out of the cleaned version.
clean.opHint.duplicate_column: A copy of a column, beside it.
clean.opHint.assemble_date: One date from a year, a month and a day held in separate columns (an hour and a minute too). The part columns stay.
clean.opHint.label_rows: A text column with the label of each pinned row (Advanced · Pinned rows); the other rows empty, or the value you give. The rows are those of the current import: after a re-import, add the labels again (R-PIN-15).
clean.opHint.set_cells: Given cells of a column get a value (a label corrected, an empty cell filled, an error fixed), the rows by their number in the file. Made by More checks; on another file it does not apply.
clean.opHint.drop_rows: Rows removed by their number in the file. Made by More checks; on another file it does not apply.
clean.opHint.change_type: Write a column as numbers, dates, true/false or text, with its format.
clean.opHint.normalize_spaces: Trim the ends, one space between words (tabs, no-break spaces).
clean.opHint.remove_invisible: Zero-width spaces, byte-order marks, control characters.
clean.opHint.change_case: lower case, UPPER CASE or Title Case.
clean.opHint.replace_values: Replace an exact value, a piece of text or a pattern (regular expression).
clean.opHint.map_values: A table old value → new value; also merges spellings.
clean.opHint.fill: Empty cells take the value above (down) or below (up).
clean.opHint.fill_empty: Empty cells take a value you give.
clean.opHint.null_outside: Numbers below a minimum or above a maximum become empty.
clean.opHint.pad_zeros: Codes that lost their leading zeros get them back (5207 → 05207).
clean.opHint.filter_rows: Keep or remove the rows matching conditions.
clean.opHint.drop_duplicates: Rows equal on the chosen columns (all by default): keep one.
clean.opHint.drop_empty_rows: Rows with no value at all.
clean.opHint.drop_header_rows: Rows repeating the column names (files pasted together).
clean.opHint.transform_number: Round, absolute value, multiply or divide, clip to a range, or group into bins of a width.
clean.opHint.split_column: New columns from the parts of a column: at a delimiter, at positions, or where digits meet letters (12kg → 12, kg). The last part keeps the rest; the column stays.
clean.opHint.merge_columns: A new column joining several columns with a separator; empty values are left out.
clean.opHint.extract_text: The first or last characters, what lies between two markers, or what a pattern finds; in the column or in a new one.
clean.opHint.format_text: Characters on the left up to a length (zeros), then a prefix and a suffix.
clean.opHint.parse_quantity: '12 kg', '500 g', '12 x 33 cl' read as numbers in grams, litres or metres, in new columns; the unit as written in another.
clean.opHint.set_where: Give a column a value on the rows that meet conditions (country = France where city = Paris), or the result of a formula. The other rows keep theirs.
clean.opHint.conditional_column: A new column whose value depends on conditions, like a CASE WHEN.
clean.opHint.computed_column: A new column computed by a formula of the others: quantity * unit_price, round(x, 2), year(date).
clean.opHint.swap_values: Swap the values of two columns on the rows where a formula holds (an end before its start).
clean.opHint.shift_date: Move dates or times by a number of days, hours… (a negative number goes back).
clean.opHint.convert_timezone: Read times in one zone (Europe/Paris, UTC…) and write them in another; summer time follows each zone.
clean.opHint.keep_rows: The first or last rows, kept or removed, in the file's order (a footer, a test batch).
clean.opHint.promote_header: The first row becomes the column names and leaves the table (a header read as data).
clean.opHint.split_rows: One row per part of a list ("red, blue" → two rows); the other columns repeat.
clean.opHint.unpivot: Turn columns into rows: one row per column, with its name and its value (wide → long).
clean.opHint.pivot: The values of a column become columns, filled with a sum, a count… (long → wide).
clean.opHint.group_by: One row per group, with counts, sums, means… of the other columns.
clean.opHint.append_rows: The rows of another dataset added below; columns matched by name.
clean.opHint.merge_dataset: Look up columns of another dataset by a key, like a lookup: rows never multiply.
clean.describe.keepNewlines: Trim extra spaces, line breaks kept · {columns}
clean.describe.splitRows: One row per part of {column} (cut at "{delimiter}")
clean.field.why.day: Without a day, the date is the 1st of the month.
clean.field.why.other: Empty leaves the other rows empty; a value (such as none) lets ML learn pinned rows against the rest.
clean.field.formatsHint: strptime formats, separated by commas (%d/%m/%Y, %Y-%m-%d); empty: the usual ones
clean.field.why.orderBy: The row with the latest date in this column is kept (an update time); rows without a date come last.
clean.field.why.headerRow: Counted from 1 in the file's order. The rows above it leave the table with it (a note above the real header).
clean.field.why.onlyRows: Rows that do not meet every condition keep their value (a Belgian or Swiss postal code has 4 digits by nature). No condition: every row.
clean.field.keysHint: Columns, separated by commas; empty: every column
clean.field.why.decimal: The character between the whole part and the decimals.
clean.field.why.excel: Numbers from 20,000 to 60,000 read as Excel day numbers (1899-12-30 + n).
clean.field.why.mapFromRule: Kept from the rule: only these values change, a new value is never merged on its own.
clean.field.why.share: Empty: rows with no value at all. A share (50%): rows with more than this share of empty cells.
clean.field.why.positions: Where each new part starts, in characters from 1, separated by commas: one position fewer than new columns.
clean.field.why.parts: Their names, separated by commas: as many as parts; the last one keeps the rest.
clean.field.why.pattern: A regular expression (RE2); with a group in parentheses, the group is kept.
clean.field.why.quantity: Each value goes to the column of its kind, in its base unit: mg, g, kg, lb, oz → grams; ml, cl, dl, l, fl oz → litres; mm, cm, m, km → metres. '12 x 33 cl' is 3.96 litres. Leave a name empty to leave that kind out; an unknown unit stays empty.
clean.field.why.toOptional: Empty: the column itself is changed. A name: a new column beside it.
clean.field.why.cases: The first case a row meets gives its value. A case tests values (conditions), a formula, or both.
clean.field.why.formula: Columns by name ("unit price" in double quotes when it has spaces), texts in single quotes, + - * / and comparisons, and functions such as round, abs, coalesce, lower, year, date_diff. Nothing else runs.
clean.field.why.amount: A whole number; negative goes back in time.
clean.field.why.time: One column with the hour and minute: 07:40, 7h40, 0740 or 740 (read as hhmm).
clean.field.why.zone: An IANA name such as Europe/Paris, America/New_York or UTC.
clean.field.why.headers: Empty: every value found, in the order they first appear; a new value on another file makes a new column. Listed: only these, in this order.
clean.field.why.append_rows: Its rows go below these, columns matched by name; a column missing on one side is empty there.
clean.field.why.merge_dataset: Its columns are looked up by key. It must have one row per key, or the rows would multiply.
clean.field.why.sourceColumn: A new column saying which dataset each row comes from. Empty: none.
clean.field.why.joinHow: Keep every row (unmatched ones get empty cells), or only the rows found there.
clean.field.why.add: Columns of the other dataset, separated by commas.
clean.case.title: Title Case
clean.reset.label: Reset to the rule's value
clean.preview.title: What it changes
clean.preview.none: Nothing changes: no value is touched and no row is removed.
clean.preview.first: The first {count} rows touched, before and after
clean.preview.reshaped: Step {step} ({op}) reshapes the table: {before} rows → {after}. Its rows no longer come one by one from the original, so nothing is compared cell by cell: the first rows of the result are shown as they are, and the saved version has no row map (Changes then pairs rows by a key column).
clean.versions.label: Versions of this dataset
clean.versions.none: No cleaned version yet. Save the draft to make Cleaned v1.
clean.versions.name: Cleaned v{seq}
clean.versions.outOfDateHint: The dataset it was made from was reimported or retyped since.
clean.versions.deleteBody: The cleaned version is removed; the original stays as it is.
clean.cleanedNote.text: A cleaned version of this dataset exists: {name}, {steps} steps.
clean.cleanedNote.hint: The original is open. Models trained on the cleaned version learn from the fixed data; the original stays as it is.
clean.cleanedChip.hint: This is the original. {name} holds the fixed data: open this page on it. The original stays as it is.
clean.versions.recipeHint: The steps as a .clean.json file, to replay on another file.
clean.versions.rebuildHint: Run its steps again on the dataset it was made from, as it is now: makes the next cleaned version.
clean.rebuild.title: Rebuild {name}
clean.rebuild.intro: Its steps run again on {source} as it is now (reimported or retyped since). The result is a new version, {next}; {name} stays as it is. A step that no longer applies is kept, turned off, with its reason below.
clean.replay.title: Replay a cleaning on this dataset
clean.replay.intro: The steps of a cleaned version, or a recipe file, checked on this dataset: what applies, what no longer does and why, and what is new here. Nothing is saved: the steps become the draft, which you review before saving.
clean.replay.proposals: Also use columns with a close name (2 letters apart, same type)
clean.replay.checking: Replaying the steps on this dataset…
clean.replay.column.matched: {recipe} read as {column} (the same name once case and spaces are ignored)
clean.replay.column.proposed: {recipe}: the closest is {column}, used only if you allow close names
clean.replay.newColumns: New here, not in the cleaning: {columns}
clean.replay.newProblems: Found on this dataset, not in the cleaning (not applied)
clean.replay.useHint: Replaces the draft (Ctrl+Z gives it back); the steps that no longer apply stay, turned off.
clean.replay.badFile: This file is not a cleaning recipe: {error}
clean.family.label: Version of the dataset
clean.settings.title: Cleaning
clean.settings.intro: What Clean does with a new dataset. The original is never changed.
clean.settings.modeHint: Suggest only: suggestions are computed when Clean opens, the lossless ones ticked. Create a cleaned version: Cleaned v1 is made after each new import when a lossless fix changes a cell. Off: nothing is computed until you ask.
clean.settings.reliableHint: Apply the reliable fixes (the default): when Clean opens, the fixes that were right on 99% or more of the cases measured are already applied in the draft, listed first under Applied automatically, and each is undone in one click. Nothing is saved until you save a version; the original never changes. Suggest only: the fixes are listed, none applied. Create a cleaned version: the same, and Cleaned v1 is also saved after each new import when a reliable fix changes a cell. Off: nothing is computed until you ask.
clean.group.auto.hint: Reliable fixes, applied for you in the draft. Undo any you do not want; nothing is saved until you save.
clean.auto.measured: A reliable fix: right on 99% or more of the cases measured (n = {n}).
clean.auto.lossless: A reliable fix: it only removes characters that cannot be seen.
clean.changes.automatic: Steps marked automatic are the reliable fixes Clean applied by default.
clean.batch.why: The same fix on {count} columns: {columns}. One tick for all; open the line to tick them one by one and read each reason.
clean.batch.decision: the same fix on several columns: open the line to read why for each one.
clean.review.label: Review of the merge, value by value
clean.review.hint: Untick a value or a whole group that must stay apart, or change the value a group becomes. The step keeps exactly what is ticked.
clean.rows.title: Rows this fix touches
clean.rows.ticked: As the draft makes them: the steps before this one applied first.
clean.rows.unticked: Not ticked: shown as if it were, after the steps of the draft that come before it. Nothing is added to the draft.
clean.rows.dataHint: Every column of these rows, filtered by {filter}, on the dataset as it is (before any step).
clean.rows.noData: Only shown here: this fix names its rows by number, by a formula or by a test that a filter of the Data page cannot write.
shortcuts.clean.title: Clean › Suggestions
shortcuts.clean.tick: Tick or untick the fix (x too)
shortcuts.clean.open: Open it: the review of a merge or of duplicates, the columns of a batch, else its rows (e too)
shortcuts.clean.undo: Undo the last change of the draft
clean.dismiss.title: Don't suggest this again
clean.dismiss.body: A hidden suggestion is never ticked nor applied for you; its step leaves the draft. It stays listed under Dismissed, with your reason, until you suggest it again.
clean.dismiss.scope.rule: Rule {rule} on every column of this dataset
clean.dismiss.scope.column: Rule {rule} on columns named '{column}', in every dataset
clean.dismiss.notePlaceholder: A real category in this file
clean.dismissed.title: Dismissed
clean.dismissed.hint: Suggestions you asked not to see again: they are never ticked nor applied for you. The cleaning's recipe carries those of this dataset, so a replay keeps them hidden.
clean.dismissed.reach.rule: rule turned off for this dataset
clean.dismissed.reach.column: rule turned off for columns named '{column}', in every dataset
clean.dismissed.reach.everywhere: rule turned off in every dataset
clean.replay.hidden: {count} suggestions you dismissed stay hidden (the recipe carries them; Use as draft keeps them for this dataset).
clean.checks.label: Declared checks
clean.checks.intro: What must hold in this dataset, declared once: each check runs again at each import and on each new cleaned version, and a recipe takes them to the file it is replayed on, as dbt tests or Great Expectations do. A check never changes the data: it says how many rows fail and shows them.
clean.checks.none: No check yet. Add one, or use Make it a check on a step or a suggestion.
clean.checks.ran.opened: run {when}: the data changed since the last run
clean.checks.kind.sum: a total is the sum of its parts
clean.checks.kind.not_empty.hint: A row fails when one of the columns is empty (a word for 'missing' counts as empty).
clean.checks.kind.unique.hint: A row fails when its key (one to four columns) is on another row too; rows with an empty key are not counted.
clean.checks.kind.in_list.hint: A row fails when its value is not in the list; empty values pass.
clean.checks.kind.between.hint: A row fails when its value is below the lower bound or above the upper one (numbers, dates); empty values pass.
clean.checks.kind.pattern.hint: A row fails when its whole value does not match the pattern (RE2 syntax); empty values pass.
clean.checks.kind.compare.hint: A row fails when both values are filled and A does not compare to B as chosen (an end before its start).
clean.checks.kind.sum.hint: A row fails when the total differs from the sum of its parts by more than the tolerance; empty parts count as 0.
clean.checks.kind.determines.hint: Rows fail when one value of A has several values of B (a city in two countries).
clean.checks.kind.condition.hint: Every row must meet the conditions, or none may (the editor of the filter step).
clean.checks.name: Name (optional)
clean.checks.dataHint: Data opens with the filter {filter}, on the dataset as it is.
clean.checks.noData: These rows cannot be written as a filter of the Data page: they are shown here only.
clean.checks.notice: {count} declared checks fail: {rows} rows. A check changes nothing: look at the rows, then decide.
clean.checks.notice.one: {count} declared check fails: {rows} rows. A check changes nothing: look at the rows, then decide.
clean.checks.notice.errors: {count} declared checks cannot run on this dataset (a column is missing, or of another type).
clean.checks.made: Declared as check {id}: it runs at each import (Checks tab).
clean.replay.checks: The recipe's checks on this file: {summary}
clean.replay.checksAdopt: Use as draft declares them here too (those not declared yet).
clean.versions.sqlHint: The steps as one DuckDB query, each commented with its rule and where it came from. Run on the original, it gives these rows exactly.
clean.versions.pythonHint: The steps replayed with the quantilo library, without the app.
clean.journal.title: Cleaning log of {name}
clean.journal.fileHint: Who did what and when, the rules applied, the cells per column and the rows removed, to keep or share.
clean.journal.summary: {auto} steps applied automatically · {suggested} suggestions ticked · {manual} added by hand
clean.journal.none: No change of the draft was recorded: it was saved as Clean opened it.
clean.journal.draft: {count} changes of the draft since the last version
clean.journal.draftHint: They go into the next version's cleaning log when you save it.
clean.dup.label: Review of the duplicates, group by group
clean.dup.hint: Each group is the rows this fix takes for one record, as the steps before it leave them, side by side; the cells that differ are highlighted. The row kept is marked: choose another (by a rule or by hand), or untick a group whose rows are not duplicates, and all its rows stay. The step keeps exactly what you decide here.
clean.dup.notTicked: This fix is not ticked: a change here ticks it, with your choices.
clean.dup.none: No group of duplicates at this step: the steps before it changed these rows.
clean.dup.merge: Fill the kept row's empty cells from its group
clean.dup.mergeWhy: Off unless you tick it: a value from another row may be older or wrong. Ticked, each empty cell of the kept row takes the first value of the other rows of its group, in the rule's order; the groups kept whole are not touched.
clean.dup.caption: Rows of group {index}, side by side
clean.dup.allEqual: Every column is equal: exact copies.
clean.dup.moreRows: {count} more rows of this group not shown
clean.describe.dupMerge: empty cells filled from the group
clean.opHint.entity_column: One number per entity in a new column: rows whose name (case, accents and spaces aside) and anchor (a postcode, a phone, an e-mail or a key) agree share it, and so do the spellings A-20 groups. The names are not changed.
clean.field.why.anchor: A column that tells two entities of the same name apart: a postcode, a phone, an e-mail, a customer number. Two rows are one entity only when it agrees.
clean.field.entityClusters: {count} clusters of spellings from the suggestion: review them on its line.
clean.field.entityClusters#one: {count} cluster of spellings from the suggestion: review it on its line.
clean.ent.label: Review of the entities, cluster by cluster
clean.ent.hint: Each cluster is the spellings this fix gives one number in {to}, as the steps before it leave the rows, side by side with the cells of their first row; the cells that differ are highlighted. Untick a cluster whose spellings are not one entity: each keeps its own number. Tick Split off under the spellings that are another entity: together they get a number of their own. The names are never changed.
clean.ent.notTicked: This fix is not ticked: a change here ticks it, with your choices.
clean.ent.none: No cluster at this step: the steps before it changed these names.
clean.ent.tickLabel: Cluster {index}: its spellings are one entity
clean.ent.apart: not one entity: its {count} spellings keep their own numbers
clean.ent.apart#one: not one entity: its {count} spelling keeps its own number
clean.ent.split: {count} of {total} spellings split off: two numbers
clean.ent.split#one: {count} of {total} spellings split off: two numbers
clean.ent.caption: Spellings of cluster {index}, side by side
clean.ent.moreRecords: {count} more spellings of this cluster not shown
clean.ent.moreRecords#one: {count} more spelling of this cluster not shown
